arxiv-2212-03949.title: Generalized recursive atom ordering and equivalence to CL-shellability Thanks: P. Hersh is supported by NSF grant DMS-1953931.
arxiv-2212-03949.creator: Patricia Hersh, Grace Stadnyk
arxiv-2212-03949.description: Abstract . Björner and Wachs introduced CL-shellability as a technique for studying the topological structure of order complexes of partially ordered sets (posets). They also introduced the notion of recursive atom ordering, and they proved that a finite bounded poset is CL-shellable if and only if it admits a recursive atom ordering.

arxiv-2301-03979.title: Apodized photonic crystals: A non-dissipative system hosting multiple exceptional points
arxiv-2301-03979.creator: Abhishek Mondal, Shailja Sharma, Ritwick Das
arxiv-2301-03979.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Abhishek Mondal, Shailja Sharma, Ritwick Das. Optical systems obeying non-Hermitian dynamics have been the subject of intense and concerted investigation over the last two decades owing to their broad implications in photonics, acoustics, electronics as well as atomic physics. A vast majority of such investigations rely on a dissipative, balanced loss-gain system which introduces unavoidable noise and consequently, this limits the coherent control of propagation dynamics.

Wei-Lun Tsai was supported by the AMS-Simons Travel Grant. Dongxi Ye was supported by the Guangdong Basic and Applied Basic Research Foundation (Grant No. 2023A15150102
arxiv-2410-19289.creator: Mark van Hoeij, Wei-Lun Tsai, and Dongxi Ye
arxiv-2410-19289.description:
A 2024 arXiv research paper by Mark van Hoeij, Wei-Lun Tsai, and Dongxi Ye. In this work, we establish modular parameterizations for two general formulas for 1 π \frac{1}{\pi} that subsume conjectural Ramanujan type formulas due to Z.-W. Sun, which have remained open since 2011. As an application of this, in a conceptual way we interpret how Sun’s conjectural formulas arise and can be verified, as well as recover other cases that were proved by Cooper, Wan and Zudilin. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification

pmc-11359310.title: A Comparative Study on the Antidiabetic Activity, Cytotoxicity and Lipid Profile of Trichilia emetica Oils
pmc-11359310.creator: Mohammed Aldholmi, Ebtihal Althomali, Fatema Aljishi, Rizwan Ahmad, Aljawharah Alqathama, Deema Alaswad, Cheng-Yang Huang
pmc-11359310.description: The Trichilia emetica plant is traditionally used for medicinal and food purposes. However, there are limited studies on the bioactivity and cytotoxicity of its seed butter and aril oil. This study aimed to assess the antidiabetic activity and cytotoxicity of seed butter and aril oil, obtained via two different extraction methods, and compare their lipid profiles.

pmc-11430440.title: Leucocyte Telomere Length and Lung Cancer Risk: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Prospective Studies
pmc-11430440.creator: Roberto Fabiani, Manuela Chiavarini, Patrizia Rosignoli, Irene Giacchetta, Izumi Horikawa
pmc-11430440.description: Simple SummaryTelomere length (TL) may influence the carcinogenesis process. Short telomeres lead to genomic instability, which is an important event in tumor initiation, while long telomeres may promote cell division and immortality influencing tumor promotion/progression. Despite the numerous observational epidemiological studies available, the association between TL in leukocytes (LTL) and lung cancer risk is currently still uncertain.

pmc-11474822.title: Cross-Linked Polyolefins: Opportunities for Fostering Circularity Throughout the Materials Lifecycle
pmc-11474822.creator: Alison
pmc-11474822.description: Cross-linked polyolefins (XLPOs) constitute a significant portion of the plastics commercial market, with a market size of a similar order of magnitude to those of polystyrene and polyethylene terephthalate. However, few aspects of XLPO materials circularity have been examined relative to thermoplastic polyolefins.

pmc-11509487.title: Depressive Symptoms and Gut Microbiota after Bowel Preparation and Colonoscopy: A Pre–Post Intervention Study
pmc-11509487.creator: Amelia J McGuinness, Martin O’Hely, Douglas Stupart, David Watters, Samantha L Dawson, Christopher Hair, Michael Berk, Mohammadreza Mohebbi, Amy Loughman, Glenn Guest, Felice N Jacka, José Luiz de Brito Alves, Helioswilton Sales-Campos
pmc-11509487.description: Mechanical bowel preparation (MBP) is essential for visualisation of the colon during colonoscopy. Previous studies have identified changes in gut microbiota composition after MBP and colonoscopy. Considering the gut microbiota is increasingly implicated in psychiatry, we explored the potential impact of this intervention on mood and the microbiota–gut–brain axis.

pmc-12659422.description: The development of sustainable smart packaging materials has driven interest in chitosan (CS) films, reinforced with conducting polymers. In the present work, poly­(1-naphthylamine) (PNA) was incorporated into CS matrix at low weight fractions (0.15–1.0 wt %) of PNA to produce composite films with enhanced mechanical and antibacterial performance.

pmc-12730824.description: AbstractObjectivesTo develop and validate a simple risk score for predicting major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in coronary artery disease (CAD) patients using routinely available clinical variables.DesignThis was a cohort study with retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data.SettingThis study was conducted at a tertiary care centre in China.

pmc-12749837.title: Quadruple parametric optical mapping to measure cardiac metabolism-excitation-contraction coupling
pmc-12749837.creator: Amber Mills, Sharon Ann George
pmc-12749837.description: Metabolism-excitation-contraction coupling (MECC) refers to the interdependent facets of cardiac physiology working synchronously to generate each heartbeat. Simultaneous imaging of MECC parameters: transmembrane potential (Vm), intracellular calcium (Ca2+) and metabolic markers (NADH, FAD), provides a wholistic picture of cardiac physiology.

pmc-12752859.title: Psychological Indices and Health‐Related Quality of Life in Renal Replacement Therapy: A Three Groups Cross‐Sectional Study
pmc-12752859.creator: Maryam Emadzadeh, Negar Morovatdar, Mohammad Javad Mojahedi, Majid Reza Erfanian Taghvaei, Fatemeh Moharreri, Fatemeh Nazemian, Ali Emadzadeh, Mohammad Khajedaluee
pmc-12752859.description: BackgroundChronic kidney disease (CKD) is a significant global health concern. Patients in the last stage of CKD, also known as end stage kidney disease (ESKD), need to use one of the methods of renal replacement therapy including hemodialysis (HD), peritoneal dialysis (PD), and kidney transplantation (KT). ESKD adversely affects physical and mental health, as well as overall quality of life.

pmc-13010534.title: From esophagus to colon: A narrative review of eosinophilic gastrointestinal disorders
pmc-13010534.creator: Abeer Qasim, George S Zacharia, FNU Veena, Sameer D Kandhi, Harish Patel
pmc-13010534.description: Eosinophilic gastrointestinal disorders (EGID) are a heterogeneous group of chronic diseases characterized by excessive infiltration of eosinophils in the gastrointestinal tract in the absence of identifiable secondary causes. Primary EGID includes eosinophilic esophagitis, eosinophilic gastroenteritis, and eosinophilic colitis. The purpose of this review is to provide a concise overview of the current understanding and management of EGID.

pmc-13223211.title: AI-augmented communication improves HIV PrEP initiation and persistence in populations disproportionately impacted by HIV
pmc-13223211.creator: Aditya Narayan, Michael Blasingame, Sam Warmuth, Gabriella Palmeri, India Halm, Ramin Bastani, Whitney Engeran-Cordova, Harold J Phillips, Leandro Mena, Nirav R Shah
pmc-13223211.description: This retrospective cohort study evaluated an AI-powered chatbot used for PrEP support across AIDS Healthcare Foundation clinics in the United States. Among 155,217 eligible adults, individuals who engaged with the chatbot had higher rates of PrEP initiation, follow-up attendance, and appointment adherence than non-users. Engagement was greatest among younger and racial or ethnic minority patients.
